messages:
maya.lin: Spotting weird steady GPU mem growth on canary that looks like a leak but only under high concurrency. Started after kernel-picker heuristic flip yesterday.

igor.petrov: same. p95 goes up over hours until OOM on the 8-GPU box. Not reproducible on small local runs.

samir: quick notes — allocation graph shows many short-lived workspace allocations in the same size bucket, but retention persists between requests. suspect allocator fragmentation vs retained per-stream buffers.

maya.lin: repro script I used: 
```bash
# repro.sh
python tools/repro_concurrency.py --model rwl-2.7b --batch-size 1 --concurrency 48 --seq 1024 --duration 30m
```
It reliably ramps in ~20–30m on the staging 8xA100.

igor.petrov: ran nsys snapshot: `nsys profile -o kernelws --trace=cuda,cudnn python tools/repro_concurrency.py ...`
Attached mem snapshots show repeated `cuMemAlloc`/`cuMemFree` pairs but overall used bytes never drop. nvtx spans show kernel selection path toggling between `X_kernel_v2` and `X_kernel_fast` when sequence length crosses 512.

maya.lin: paste of memstat tail during ramp: 
```
GPU0: total=40536MB used=31200MB free=932MB processes=12
GPU0: total=40536MB used=31728MB free=464MB processes=12
GPU0: total=40536MB used=31840MB free=344MB processes=12
...
```
We see ~500MB increments over minutes.

priya: theory: some kernels request a transient workspace via runtime->alloc_workspace(size) and we have a path that caches per-kernel workspace pointer per device/stream but the key uses kernel_id + stream_id hash that changed after kernel-picker returns different kernel id causing both to be cached (old + new) -> growth.

samir: I repro'd a similar failure locally when forcing alternating kernel selection using env var `FORCE_KERNEL_TOGGLE=1`. When toggling, incremental resident growth appears, stops when we pin kernel variant to one id.

igor.petrov: logs from allocator: 
```
[allocator] reserve_workspace device=0 stream=7 size=2621440 ttl=0 cached=true key=K_X_v1
[allocator] reserve_workspace device=0 stream=7 size=2621440 ttl=0 cached=true key=K_X_v2
```
Two distinct keys for same logical kernel. ttl=0 means no expiry.

maya.lin: quick mitigation idea: clamp workspace cache to N entries per kernel family rather than per kernel-id, or introduce expiry/last-used LRU for stream-scoped caches. Also set default ttl=5m for transient workspaces.

priya: we also saw fragmentation fingerprint: many 2.5MB blocks in free list and no big contiguous block for a new larger kernel leading to additional cuMemAlloc that increases resident. So mix of fragmentation + logical duplicate caching.

samir: proposed short PR: change workspace key to include normalized kernel family name (strip variant suffix), and set default ttl=300s for workspace cache. I sketched code: 
```python
# allocator.py (sketch)
def workspace_key(kernel):
    return (kernel.family, device, stream_id)
```
Will run soak.

igor.petrov: action items:
- samir to push wip PR with unit tests for key normalization (ETA EOD)
- maya to run full nsys + cuda-memcheck trace on staging with kernel toggle (ETA tomorrow morning)
- priya to add a short-term server-side config to set workspace_ttl=300s for canary (done?)

deploy-bot: env change applied to canary: `WORKSPACE_TTL=300` by priya at 1912345720 :rocket:

maya.lin: thanks — I'll run the profile now and post snapshots.

samir: PR up: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/3421 (wip) includes LRU eviction and family-keying, tests + docs.

igor.petrov: if PR stabilizes mem under toggle we'll backport to hotfix branch, otherwise fallback to forcing kernel-picker to prefer one variant for now.

priya: note for postmortem: add a test in perf-ci that toggles kernel variants under concurrency to catch regressions.

maya.lin: update — after TTL applied the ramp slowed a lot, p95 stable for 2h so far. Looks promising. :thumbsup:

samir: will push refined PR tomorrow and run long soak.

maya.lin: leaving logs and nsys dump under //artifacts/leak_triage/1912345678/ for anyone who wants to dig in.

igor.petrov: great thread. saved us a hairy outage.
